correctness.rationale: For 0<epsilon<1 and the small zero-drift/zero-phase graph, M_epsilon(0)=0 and the fiber slope r=(1-epsilon)/(1+epsilon) lies in (0,1); the contraction/implicit-function argument gives uniform parameter derivative. The exact cohomological response has Fibonacci wavevectors B^n e1=(F_(2n-1),-F_(2n)) and weights r^(n-1), with |B^n e1| comparable to lambda^n. Fourier Parseval yields H^s iff r*lambda^s<1 including endpoint divergence. Uniform derivative sums give C^m sufficiency, and Riemann-Lebesgue for the t-derivative excludes all m>=1 at and beyond r*lambda^m=1. The s-derivative sum attains its absolute maximum at the origin and the even Fibonacci generating function gives 2pi/(1-3r+r^2). No claim for nonlinear finite forcing.
